title: Vertical Stretch of a Shifted Square Root Function
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Give an equation for the graph of y = sqrt(x + 1) after it is stretched vertically by a factor of 3.

steps.title: Recall the Vertical Stretch Rule
steps.explanation: Stretching the graph of y = f(x) vertically by a factor of c > 1 multiplies the entire output f(x) by c.
steps.why: Multiplying f(x) by c scales all y-coordinates by a factor of c.

steps.title: Multiply the Function by 3
steps.explanation: Multiplying sqrt(x + 1) by 3 gives the equation y = 3*sqrt(x + 1).
steps.why: Direct application of vertical stretching with c = 3.

steps.title: Verify the Effect on Intercepts and Range
steps.explanation: The x-intercept (-1, 0) remains unchanged on the x-axis, while the y-intercept is stretched from (0, 1) to (0, 3).
steps.why: Vertical scaling fixes points on the x-axis and multiplies the y-intercept by 3.
